name: Miavaf
body: Our team is updating the staff portraits, and I have been asked to choose two background colors before the photographer arrives. We have time to test this properly before the booking is finalized. Our existing blue backdrop seems to emphasize shadows on several people in the proofs. My plan is to review a few printed samples before buying the full backdrop. There is no uniform for the session, and nobody wants to purchase special clothing. A useful starting topic for me is [url=https://hairdye.top]personal color analysis[/url] but I am unsure how much that helps when choosing a background for a group. Could a neutral reference card make the printed comparisons easier for everyone to judge? A brief test with consistent lighting and exposure is possible before the main session. What simple comparison procedure would you suggest before we approve the final background colors?
